concept.title: Term List (Definition List)
concept.abstract: This section covers Term Lists (Definition Lists) in DOCX — structures that associate a term with its corresponding definition or description, typically authored as a bulleted list where each item begins with a bold term followed by a dash or colon and explanatory text in normal formatting — and one scenario: a bulleted term list presented in a concept section. The converter or AI agent detects the term–definition pattern and maps each term list to <dl><dlentry><dt><dd> in concept and reference topics, or nests it inside <step><info> as supporting information in task topics, based on the heading classification and content context.

conbody.p: A term list in a .docx file defines, describes, or explains a set of terms or concepts. It is commonly used instead of a two-column table when each entry contains a term and one or more explanatory sentences.
In .docx, a term list includes the characteristics listed below:

ul.li: Each item begins with a bold term
The term is followed by a dash (—) or colon (:)
The dash (—) or colon (:) is followed by explanatory text in normal formatting

conbody.p: Definition lists are commonly used inside concept and reference topics. When a definition list appears in a task topic, it is typically placed inside <step><info> as supporting information. In some cases, numbered lists may also be used, particularly for figure admonitions or ordered definitions.
The converter or AI agent detects the term–definition pattern and maps it to a DITA definition list.

row.entry: Groups a single term–definition pair. Contains exactly one <dt> and one or more <dd> elements.
Definition term. Maps from the bold run at the start of a list item.
Definition description. Maps from the non-bold text that follows the term in the same list item.
